question: At supratherapeutic doses, barbiturates can open the GABA-A Cl⁻ channel directly without requiring GABA to be present, which is why they can cause fatal respiratory depression without a pharmacological ceiling.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Unlike benzodiazepines (which absolutely require GABA to be present), barbiturates at high concentrations activate the Cl⁻ channel directly. This eliminates any ceiling on respiratory depression — the basis for their narrow therapeutic index and lethal overdose potential without a reversal agent.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This direct (GABA-independent) channel opening at high doses removes the ceiling on CNS depression. There is no specific reversal agent for barbiturate overdose — management is entirely supportive (airway protection, ventilation). This property is the primary reason barbiturates have been replaced by benzodiazepines for most indications.
